deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §4, 'Mesures spectrales et sous-espaces spectraux d'opérateurs'. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1953 work on rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with a trace. The previous page deals with 'fonctions de Weyl' (rearrangement or distribution-type functions) and inequalities W(f) ≤ W(g). That material became the Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace' (1955). This page sets up the noncommutative measure theory those inequalities need.

Setup:
- 𝒜 is a von Neumann algebra (a weakly closed involutive operator algebra on a Hilbert space).
- A trace T is a map 𝒜^+ → [0, +∞] that is additive and positively homogeneous (with 0·∞ = 0) and unitarily invariant.
- Standard facts (Dixmier 1952–53): the set {A ≥ 0 : T(A) < ∞} is the positive part of a two-sided ideal 𝔞, the 'idéal de définition'. T extends to a linear form on 𝔞, and T(AB) = T(BA) for A ∈ 𝔞 and B ∈ 𝒜.

Definitions given:
- Semi-finite: every A > 0 dominates some B with 0 < B ≤ A and T(B) < ∞.
- Normal: T(sup A_i) = sup T(A_i) for every bounded increasing filtering family.
- For normal T, semi-finite is equivalent to 𝔞 being dense in 𝒜.
- Faithful: T(A) = 0 with A ≥ 0 implies A = 0.

From here on, 𝒜 carries a fixed faithful normal semi-finite trace T. The last line introduces 𝔟, most plausibly the norm closure of 𝔞, a closed involutive two-sided ideal.

The next page shows the purpose of 𝔟:
- 𝔟 = 𝒜 if and only if 𝔞 = 𝒜, i.e. T is finite.
- For normal A ∈ 𝔟 and f a bounded Borel function vanishing near 0, f(A) ∈ 𝔞. In particular the spectral projections E_{|λ|>ε} have finite trace.

So 𝔟 is the ideal of 'T-compact' operators, the noncommutative analogue of the compact operators (or of functions 'vanishing at infinity' in measure). The point is to have spectral measures with finite-trace tails, so that distribution functions and decreasing rearrangements (generalized s-numbers) can be defined for these operators.
errors: 'son idéal de définition est dense' must mean dense for the weak (σ-weak/strong) topology. Norm density is false: for B(H) with the usual trace, the finite-rank/trace-class ideal is not norm dense.
Semi-finiteness is written with strict 0<B<A. The intended (standard) condition is B ≠ 0 with B ≤ A; a minor imprecision.
'Famille filtrante croissante majorée' is needed for sup to exist in 𝒜^+; correctly stated, no error.

ideas.what: Trace on a von Neumann algebra: ideal of definition, linear extension, T(AB)=T(BA), normal/semi-finite/faithful traces
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace' (preliminaries)

ideas.what: Norm closure 𝔟 of the definition ideal; characterization: f(A) ∈ 𝔞 for bounded Borel f vanishing near 0 (finite-trace spectral tails); 𝔟 = 𝒜 iff T finite
ideas.modern_name: ideal of τ-compact operators (relative compact operators in a semifinite von Neumann algebra)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Breuer (1968–69, Fredholm theory in von Neumann algebras); later Fack–Kosaki (1986), Kaftal
ideas.where_published: possibly implicit in the 1955 Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck explicitly introduces the norm-closed ideal of 'T-compact' operators in a von Neumann algebra with an f.n.s. trace. He proves that their spectral projections away from 0 have finite trace, as the basis for spectral/rearrangement theory. This anticipates Breuer's relative compact operators (1968) and the τ-compact operators of Fack–Kosaki. Grothendieck's Bourbaki exposé is sometimes cited by Fack–Kosaki, so the priority is partly on record, but this explicit ideal-theoretic setup may not be.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical-priority detail for noncommutative integration and singular-value theory, not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of standard definitions of traces on von Neumann algebras (Dixmier) plus the start of a τ-compact ideal construction. That construction is early, but the surrounding rearrangement theory was published by Grothendieck in 1955 and is known to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Mesures spectrales et sous-espaces spectraux d'opérateurs' — the '[?]' is unnecessary.

Last lines likely read 'Soit 𝔟 l'adhérence de 𝔞 pour la topologie de la norme, ... l'idéal bilatère involutif ...' (norm closure of 𝔞), rather than 'l'ensemble de 𝔞 formé des ...'. This is consistent with the next page's 'b = A iff a = A'.
'fidèle T' is duplicated in the machine transcription; it is a single insertion ('trace normale semi-finie fidèle T').
